Bulk-expanded AI-generated prose often contains generic placeholder paragraphs that undermine reader engagement. ### Quality pass procedure 1. **Load the `manuscript-preparation-and-delivery` skill** and use its `references/generic-paragraph-detection.md` for the full list of generic phrase patterns 2. **Scan the book's HTML** for these patterns: - "The work continued through the long hours" - "In the silence of the habitat" - "The data painted a complex picture" - `"We're making progress," someone reported` - "The implications were staggering" - (full list in the detection reference) 3. **Replace each generic block** with character-driven content: named characters, sensory specifics, dialogue with subtext, emotional stakes. Each replacement should advance the plot or deepen character. 4. **Verify zero generic phrases remain** (allowing for false positives in dialogue) 5. **Verify structural integrity** — chapter headings, TOC, copyright, back matter all still present See `manuscript-preparation-and-delivery/references/generic-paragraph-detection.md` for the bulk replacement script template and before/after examples. ## Step 1: Pre-Publish Review Proof After the quality pass, generate a **content-only review PDF** (no cover artwork) for the author to do a read-through. This catches content and formatting issues before investing time in the full packaging. ### When to use - Author says "send me a review copy" or "I need to read through it first" - Before finalizing cover design — content should be locked first - Before delivering the KDP package ### How to build #### A) From existing print-formatted HTML ```bash weasyprint output/{BOOK_KEY}.html output/{BOOK_KEY}_Review.pdf # Verify: 150-200 pages at 6×9in (432×648 pts), all chapters present ``` If the HTML has embedded cover art: ```bash sed '/data:image/d' output/{BOOK_KEY}.html > output/{BOOK_KEY}_Review_Clean.html weasyprint output/{BOOK_KEY}_Review_Clean.html output/{BOOK_KEY}_Review.pdf ``` #### B) From raw markdown manuscript (no existing HTML) When starting from a `.md` manuscript, you need to build HTML first. **Always detect the heading format first** — manuscripts do not use a consistent heading level for chapters: **Common heading patterns found across manuscripts:** | Pattern | Example | Frequency | |---------|---------|-----------| | `# Chapter N: Title` | `# Chapter One: The Shock` | Common | | `## Chapter N — Title` | `## Chapter 1 — The Observatory Rising` | Very common | | `## Chapter N: Title` | `## Chapter 1: The Welcome Fleet` | Common | | `# CHAPTER N — TITLE` | `# CHAPTER ONE — BUILT FROM DUST` | Occasional | | `## N. Title` | `## 1. The Artemis Accord` | Rare | | `### Chapter N` | `### Chapter 1` | Rare | **Detection command:** ```bash # Show all unique heading patterns in the manuscript grep -n '^#' manuscript.md | head -30 # Count total chapters grep -c '^## Chapter\|^# Chapter\|^## [0-9]' manuscript.md ``` **Build the review HTML from markdown:** Write a Python script that: 1. Reads the manuscript line-by-line 2. Detects chapter headings (handle both `#` and `##` level headings that contain "Chapter") 3. Wraps each chapter in `

` with `page-break-before: always` 4. Adds title page, copyright page, TOC (list of chapter titles as links), and "About the Author" back matter 5. Applies 6×9in print CSS **Python f-string warning:** When generating HTML via Python in Hermes, use `chr(10).join()` instead of `"\\n".join()` inside f-strings. Python 3.11 (Hermes' runtime) does not allow backslash characters inside f-string `{}` expressions: ```python # WRONG — SyntaxError: x = f'
{"\\n".join(items)}
' # RIGHT: x = f'
{chr(10).join(items)}
' ``` **CSS template for review PDFs:** ```css @page { size: 6in 9in; margin: 0.75in; @bottom-center { content: counter(page); font-size: 9pt; color: #888; } } body { font-family: Georgia, 'Times New Roman', serif; line-height: 1.5; font-size: 11pt; } .title-page { text-align: center; padding-top: 30%; } .title-page h1 { font-size: 1.8em; page-break-before: avoid; } h1 { text-align: center; page-break-before: always; font-size: 1.3em; } p { margin: 0.2em 0; text-indent: 1.2em; widows: 2; orphans: 2; } ``` #### C) Preferred — PNG→JPEG for illustrations Replace base64 images with local file paths instead of stripping them. Base64 images are 5× their binary size and slow WeasyPrint to a crawl (a 5-image HTML can be 16+ MB). Convert to `file:///absolute/path/to/image.jpg` references BEFORE creating the review PDF. If the PNG files are large (~750KB each for 1024×1024), convert them to JPEG quality 75-80 to shrink to ~240KB each with negligible visual loss for sketches. #### D) TOC page numbers — hardcode after first pass Replace `target-counter` TOC page numbers with **hardcoded numbers** after the first render pass — `target-counter` is unreliable when long chapter titles wrap (the page number floats to the wrong line). Render → extract actual page numbers via `pdftotext` → hardcode → re-render. #### E) Parallel generation for book series When processing multiple books in a series (e.g., all 5 "No Blue Sky" books), **delegate each book to a separate subagent** via `delegate_task` with parallel tasks. Each subagent independently reads their manuscript and generates the PDF. Max concurrent children defaults to 3 — batch books in groups of 3+2 if needed. ### Verify the review PDF ```bash pdfinfo output/{BOOK_KEY}_Review.pdf | grep -E 'Pages|Page size' pdftotext output/{BOOK_KEY}_Review.pdf - | grep -c "Chapter" # confirm all chapters present ``` **Page count targeting:** If your book is too short or too long for the target page range (e.g., 180-200 pages at 6×9in), you can adjust the **typography density** (font-size, line-height, margins) to expand or compress the text. See `references/page-count-targeting.md` for the density reference table, CSS knob strengths, and a quick-estimation formula. Apply a different density per book when building a multi-volume series with uneven word counts. **Checklist for author review:** - [ ] All chapters present (count them in the PDF) - [ ] No front cover artwork (just text title page) - [ ] No back cover content - [ ] TOC lists everything - [ ] Page count is reasonable (150-200 for a trade book) - [ ] Final paragraph / closing reflection is present ### Pitfall - WeasyPrint base64 images inside HTML can bloat files to 5MB+. Build KDP Package Create `build_kdp_package.py` in the book directory. It should: **a) Kindle/** - Copy the EPUB from `output/` - Copy (or generate) the 1600×2560 Kindle cover JPEG **b) Print/** - Read the existing HTML output - Inject KDP print CSS (6.25×9.25in page with 0.125in bleeds, bleeds margin) - Regenerate PDF via WeasyPrint - Generate wrap cover image (front + spine + back): - Spine width: `pages * 0.00225` (cream paper) or `pages * 0.00252` (white) - Total width: `6.0*2 + spine + 0.125*2` inches - Total height: `9.0 + 0.125*2` inches - At 300 DPI, paste front cover on right, back cover (darkened) on left, spine text centered - Save as JPEG and PDF **c) Marketing_and_Compliance/** - `Book_Description.md` — compelling description (2-3 paragraphs) - `Author_Bio.md` — 2-3 sentence bio - `Categories_and_Keywords.md` — 4 suggested BISAC categories, 7 keywords - `KDP_AI_Disclosure.md` — if AI was used in manuscript generation **d) README.md** — submission instructions for the author **e) ZIP** — archive the entire package ### 4. Deliver to Telegram Send via MEDIA: links: - The `{BOOK_KEY}_KDP_PACKAGE.zip` (full package, under 20MB) - Individual key files as needed ### 5. Save this Skill After completing and noting any issues, patch this skill with fixes. ## KDP Kindle EPUB Requirements (per Kindle Publishing Guidelines 2025.1) **Supporting files:** - `references/kdp-guidelines-sources.md` — all official KDP help topic URLs - `templates/kdp-epub-style.css` — KDP-safe CSS template (no ::before/::after, no counter-*, no img selector) When building the EPUB for Kindle submission, it must comply with Amazon's Kindle Publishing Guidelines.
